source: Main-text Figure 1 and Supplementary Material S2.2

branches.question: Who scored higher?
branches.label: Person-level score
aligned_evidence: Alpha/KR-20 attached to one exact score unit: time point, condition, subtest, item set, denominator, and scoring rule
Score distribution, floor and ceiling rates, zero-variance item count, and SEM
Item-deletion rule and item count before and after deletion, when applicable
minimum_reporting: Define the exact score unit and eligible denominator before naming a coefficient.
Report the coefficient with item count, mean, SD, SEM, floor/ceiling rates, and zero-variance items.
Keep coefficients separate when time point, condition, subtest, item set, or scoring rule changes.
does_not_license: Generalization beyond the sampled words or learners
Validity of the task, distractors, scoring rule, or testing schedule
branches.reporting_starter: For the exact [time × condition × subtest × item set × scoring rule] score, report alpha/KR-20, k, M, SD, SEM, floor/ceiling rates, zero-variance items, the eligible denominator, and any item-deletion rule. Interpret the coefficient only as evidence about learner ranking for that defined score.

branches.question: Which condition worked?
branches.label: Condition effect
aligned_evidence: Item-level GLMM or explanatory IRT with the prespecified condition contrast
Fixed effect or contrast with uncertainty, participant/item variance terms, and convergence or boundary diagnostics
Word-condition assignment or counterbalancing and, for between-group designs, baseline equivalence or adjustment
minimum_reporting: State assignment, sampling, observation, and analysis units separately.
Report the model formula, contrast coding, effect estimate, SE or interval, variance components, and diagnostics.
Report response-scale descriptives without substituting them for model-based uncertainty.
does_not_license: Repair of confounding by a high alpha/KR-20 value
Automatic generalization to new words, learners, classes, schools, or prefectures
A claim that unsupported random slopes or dependence structures were estimated
branches.reporting_starter: Report the condition contrast from an item-level model, its uncertainty, the participant/item terms, coding, convergence and singularity diagnostics, and the assignment/counterbalancing evidence. Treat score alpha/KR-20 as auxiliary rather than as evidence for the treatment effect.

branches.question: Would it hold for other words or learners?
branches.label: Effect generalizability
branches.inferential_target: Stability of the effect beyond sampled words or learners
aligned_evidence: Item-by-condition and, where relevant, learner-by-condition variability
Resampling over the population to which the claim extends
A G-study/D-study-style projection that keeps tested items, learned words, exposure time, and item count distinct
minimum_reporting: Name every population over which the effect is intended to generalize.
Report the corresponding random-slope SD, resampling result, or design-projection inputs and uncertainty.
Narrow the claim when the design or fitted model omits a required generalization facet.
does_not_license: Item-sample generalizability from alpha/KR-20 at any value
A universal effect from one sampled word list or one assigned class
Power, coverage, or exact future-study performance from an analytic sensitivity projection
branches.reporting_starter: State whether the effect is intended to generalize over learners, words, or both; report the corresponding condition-slope variability, resampling, or D-study-style projection. Keep tested items, learned words, exposure time, and item count distinct, and narrow any population claim not supported by the design.

branches.question: What counted as knowledge?
branches.label: Design / scoring
aligned_evidence: Task and scoring rationale tied to strict, lenient, partial-credit, recognition, or composite responses
Format-specific evidence such as distractor quality, guessing, scorer training, or adjudication
No-test, delayed-only, parallel-form, test-only, or control-item evidence when repeated testing is part of the claim
minimum_reporting: State what response earns each score and why that response represents the intended knowledge state.
Report denominator, exclusions, filler/control-item handling, and format-specific diagnostics.
For delayed-retention claims, describe the testing schedule and evidence separating retention from test-induced learning.
does_not_license: Construct validity from a high alpha/KR-20 value
Equivalence of strict, lenient, partial-credit, and recognition scores
A delayed-retention interpretation when repeated testing is uncontrolled or unreported
branches.reporting_starter: Define the response and scoring criteria, eligible denominator, exclusions, and treatment of filler/control items. Add format-specific diagnostics and, when retention is claimed, describe the testing schedule and controls that separate intervention effects from repeated-test exposure.
